decision.case_state: Quote recorded (Q-101, £605 sum of items, VAT unstated). Landlord approval requested at event 013 and re-asked; no landlord reply. Provider's claim of phone approval is hearsay. Ticket on hold until 2024-10-14.

next_actions.action: Ask landlord for a written yes/no on the £605 quote, noting the provider's phone claim
Hold for landlord reply, review 2024-10-14 (second-channel chase then)

boundaries: Recording the quote does not approve it
Telling the provider not to order does not decline the work
No contractor instruction or spend committed
remaining_work: Provider to confirm VAT and a visit/start date
Then approve quote, record decision, schedule work, invoice, close
decision.summary: Provider Sawyer says the landlord approved the £605 quote by phone and plans to order materials. That is hearsay, so I recorded the quote, told Sawyer not to order, asked the landlord for written yes/no and put the job on hold to 14 Oct.

answers.question: Where does this case stand right now, and what is outstanding?
answers.answer: Quote received and recorded; landlord approval is outstanding. Provider's verbal-approval claim is not accepted. VAT unconfirmed.

answers.question: What is the next action, who is it for, and through which channel?
answers.answer: Landlord (Oscar) asked by email for a written yes/no; provider told to wait by email; hold until 2024-10-14 then chase on SMS/phone.

answers.question: Does anything need a human decision, and why?
answers.answer: No. Routine waiting on landlord approval; escalate only if the landlord stays silent after the chase.
